description: A general-purpose DEFLATE codec: raw/zlib/gzip stream decoding, a Huffman table builder, a checksum layer and a buffered stdio-style file layer. The base is a well-known upstream library, so de-identification is mandatory and the injected defects sit at sites we chose rather than at any site an advisory describes.
attacker_controls: every byte of the compressed stream handed to the decoder, including all header fields, block types, code-length lists, stored-block lengths, match lengths and distances, and the trailer; for the file layer, the whole file content and (in an unpacking scenario) the member name used for error messages

base._files_note: Only the root translation units and their private headers. crc32.h is deliberately excluded: it is a 9.4k-line generated table of hexadecimal constants, and the tree is built with the runtime table generator instead (see build.cflags and base.extra_files). test/, contrib/, examples/ and the per-platform directories are excluded because none of them compiles standalone.
base._extra_files_note: Rendered through the identifier map, so the two feature macros come out under the same pseudonyms the tree uses. That is why the flags are not passed as -D: a -D on the command line would name the original macro, which both defeats the renaming and leaves the original spelling sitting in build.sh.

deidentify._reserved_extra_note: Three groups. (1) Preprocessor directive keywords: the de-identifier renames identifiers in code regions and #define/#ifdef/#endif/#elif/#undef/#pragma/#error are not in its reserved list, so without these the whole tree turns into 'invalid preprocessing directive'. (2) <stdatomic.h> names the reserved list does not carry, used by the runtime CRC table's once() guard. (3) The token that the identifier regex finds inside a hexadecimal literal: 0xffff scans as the identifier 'xffff', which the renamer would rewrite to '0nubvax'. Reserving the 36 distinct hex tails that occur in the selected files is the only way to keep integer literals intact without editing the harness. 'main' is reserved because crc32.c carries a MAKECRCH-only main() and renaming it would rename the smoke test's entry point too.
deidentify._string_scrub_note: Identifier renaming already rewrites the project's symbols where they appear inside string literals, so the wire error messages lose their distinctive nouns for free. These patterns cover what is left: the author names and the copyright years, the version triple, and the three file stems that only ever appear inside literals (zlib.h, trees.h, inffixed.h) and so are never reached by the include rewriter.

entry_points.why: the stream decoder: every byte it consumes comes from an untrusted peer or file, and it is the function an attacker drives directly
one-shot decompression of an attacker-supplied buffer, the API most callers reach for when inflating an untrusted blob
raw-stream decoding with caller-supplied input and output callbacks, used by gzip-style unpackers on wholly untrusted input
reads and decompresses an untrusted file: the attacker controls the file's whole content, including its header fields and trailer
opens a file by a name that, when unpacking an archive or following a manifest, an attacker chose
tears down a file handle whose state was shaped entirely by attacker-controlled content and error paths
computes a checksum directly over untrusted bytes, both from the decoder and from application code validating a payload
computes the rolling checksum over untrusted bytes on every decode of a wrapped stream
